The crisis in the Strait of Hormuz is a heavy blow to the deteriorating maritime order
Elisabeth Braw — Atlantic Council issue brief, 31 July 2026

Examines how Iran's de facto blockade of Hormuz undermines UNCLOS transit passage and sets precedents for other strait states.
"Transit passage through straits was, in fact, a key objective for some of the world's most powerful countries during the UNCLOS negotiations."
"In the week before the war, 38 percent of global oil supply travelled through the Strait of Hormuz, as did 29 percent of liquefied petroleum gas."
"The seas have become an arena for geopolitical conflict, and the maritime industry has become a clear target."
"We will see backsliding in straits...there's still a variety of these strait states that would love to go the other way."
"Even if a reopening of the strait's central route is achieved in the near future...the implications of the closure would remain staggering."
